places.name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
places.note: Portaluppi's 1930s villa for an industrial family: marble, walnut, a garden with a heated pool behind tall hedges. Milanese restraint at its most luxurious.

places.name: Fondazione Prada
places.note: OMA's conversion of an old distillery, with one building dipped in gold leaf. Stay for Bar Luce, Wes Anderson's pastel café by the entrance.

places.name: San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
places.note: A plain church wall hiding a fully frescoed interior, Luini's workshop end to end. The nuns' hall behind the screen is the real surprise. Free.

places.name: Museo Poldi Pezzoli
places.note: A collector's apartment kept intact, armour downstairs and Pollaiuolo's profile portrait of a young woman upstairs. Intimate, and rarely busy.

places.name: Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano
places.note: A couple's apartment hung floor to ceiling with 20th-century Italian art, in a Portaluppi building. Free, and you may have it to yourself.

places.name: Triennale Milano
places.note: Muzio's 1933 palazzo for design, on the edge of Parco Sempione. See the design museum, then take a drink on the terrace above the park.

places.name: Studio Museo Achille Castiglioni
places.note: The great designer's studio as he left it: prototypes, found objects, toys and drawings. Seen by guided tour only; book ahead.

places.name: Armani/Silos
places.note: A former 1950s granary turned into Giorgio Armani's archive of four decades of clothes. Concrete, low light, total control.

places.name: Torre Velasca
places.note: BBPR's 1958 mushroom-shaped tower, a medieval silhouette in reinforced concrete. Best seen from the small piazza at its foot.

places.name: Bosco Verticale
places.note: Boeri's two towers planted with hundreds of trees, a forest stacked on balconies. Walk around it from the Biblioteca degli Alberi park.

places.name: Pasticceria Marchesi
places.note: A pastry shop dating from 1824, wood-panelled and mirrored. Espresso standing at the counter, a brioche, then on your way.

places.name: 10 Corso Como
places.note: The courtyard concept store Carla Sozzani founded in 1990: gallery, bookshop and garden café behind an old Milanese facade. The template many have copied since.

places.name: NAMI Hi-Fi
places.note: A new listening bar where the room is tuned before it is styled. Restored horn speakers, records chosen with care, a drink in hand. The name means 'wave'; let the evening come and go like one.

places.name: Pinacoteca di Brera
places.note: Mantegna's foreshortened Christ and Raphael's Marriage of the Virgin. The restorers' studio is behind glass.

places.name: Orto Botanico di Brera
places.note: A small walled botanic garden behind the Brera, with two ginkgo trees. Free, and almost secret.

places.name: Cimitero Monumentale
places.note: An open-air museum of tombs, from Liberty to modernist; BBPR's lattice memorial is unforgettable. Free.

places.name: GAM – Villa Reale
places.note: 19th-century Italian painting and sculpture in a neoclassical villa, with an English garden behind.

places.name: Pietà Rondanini
places.note: Michelangelo's last, unfinished sculpture, in the old Spanish hospital inside the Castello. Stand behind it.

places.name: Museo del Novecento
places.note: Italian 20th-century art in the Arengario. Pellizza's Fourth Estate greets you, then a spiral ramp climbs to Fontana's neon above the Duomo.

places.name: Casa degli Atellani
places.note: A Renaissance house with Portaluppi interiors and, in the garden, Leonardo's replanted vineyard.

places.name: San Bernardino alle Ossa
places.note: A small chapel lined with human bones in patterns, under a Rococo ceiling. Strange and beautiful.

places.name: Darsena and Navigli
places.note: The old harbour where the canals meet, now a promenade. Walk the Naviglio Grande at aperitivo hour.

places.name: Bar Basso
places.note: The bar that invented the Negroni sbagliato, served in vast glasses. A ritual during Design Week.

places.name: Camparino in Galleria
places.note: An Art Nouveau bar at the entrance to the Galleria, mosaics and all. A Campari seltz standing at the counter.

places.name: Trattoria Masuelli San Marco
places.note: A family trattoria since 1921, serving cotoletta and risotto. Old Milan without a hint of nostalgia.

places.name: Ratanà
places.note: Modern Milanese cooking in an early-20th-century building near the Bosco Verticale. The saffron risotto is the order.

places.name: Pirelli HangarBicocca
places.note: A former train factory for huge installations, including Kiefer's Seven Heavenly Palaces. Free.

places.name: Fondazione Feltrinelli
places.note: Herzog & de Meuron's long, narrow, steeply pitched glass building on the old city wall line. There's a bookshop and café.

places.name: Rossana Orlandi
places.note: A design gallery in an old tie factory, with a courtyard bar. Where new design talent is found.

places.name: The Last Supper
places.address: Piazza di Santa Maria delle Grazie
places.note: Leonardo's mural in the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie. Fifteen minutes each, booked weeks ahead.

places.name: Biblioteca Ambrosiana
places.note: Leonardo's Codex Atlanticus, Caravaggio's basket of fruit and an old reading hall. Scholarly and calm.

places.name: Torre Branca
places.note: Gio Ponti's 1933 steel lattice tower in Parco Sempione. A lift to the top on clear days.

places.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
places.note: The 1870s iron-and-glass arcade, a covered city street. Go early, before the shoppers.
